text:
alex.sr: Heads-up — we're kicking off a POC with a regulated customer (financial). They need Private/VPC deployment and have a few hard constraints: static egress IPs, preserve client source IP, and strict outbound allowlist. What's our recommended topology and any pricing delta?

priya.se: Key Qs: do they require mutual TLS to our endpoint? And are they expecting PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or VPC peering to a carrier/VPN?

alex.sr: They asked for PrivateLink to avoid cross-account peering. mTLS preferred but optional for phase 1. Main asks: 1) static egress IP for allowlisting 2) preserve client src IP for audit logs 3) firewall rules snippet we can hand to their infra team.

marvin.net: For PrivateLink we terminate in our customer VPC via an interface endpoint. Egress IPs are on our side (we can allocate EIPs from a NAT or egress proxy) — preserving original client src IP across NAT is not trivial. We can preserve client IP if traffic flows through a proxy that does X-Forwarded-For, but that changes src seen by destination unless the customer's firewall trusts that header.

dana.sec: From a security and audit perspective they want source IP preservation to map requests to internal users. We need to clarify: do they require TCP-level srcIP or is app-level identity (JWT / mTLS) acceptable?

jorge.ae: Customer says they need firewall rules at their perimeter to show exact src IPs for our service for compliance. They won't accept opaque translations without compensating controls.

priya.se: Options: (A) Preserve src IP via an L3 tunnel (VPN/Direct Connect) + TGW — avoids NAT but means peering/privatelink tradeoffs. (B) PrivateLink + EIP set where we advertise fixed EIPs (customer sees our EIPs). (C) PrivateLink + an on-customer-hosted reverse proxy (we give container image) so client IP is preserved internally.

marvin.net: Quick network rule snippet for option B (customer allowlist our EIPs):

```
# Example firewall allowlist (customer side)
# Allow traffic to Redwood inference egress addresses (TCP 443)
allow from any to 52.23.110.99/32 port 443 comment "redwood-egress-1"
allow from any to 52.23.110.100/32 port 443 comment "redwood-egress-2"
```

alex.sr: Do we have fixed EIPs we can promise for Dedicated/Private customers? Or is that an add-on?

marvin.net: For our Dedicated offering we can allocate customer-dedicated EIPs as part of the contract (we reserve a small pool). For Hosted PrivateLink endpoints it's best-effort — recommend Dedicated for strict allowlist needs. Pricing-wise, static EIP reservation is an add-on (monthly).

dana.sec: If they insist on original client src IP at the destination (not our EIP), we should propose an L3 tunnel in the POC. That requires their network team to accept BGP or a managed VPN and is slower to stand up. Also ask for SOC2/ISO attestation steps (we'll provide docs).

priya.se: POC checklist I suggest we send them:
- Confirm PrivateLink vs TGW/VPN
- Decide on static EIP reservation or L3 tunnel
- mTLS requirement for call auth
- Firewall allowlist file (we provide once EIPs assigned)
- Audit/logging format (XFF vs srcIP)
- Estimated monthly cost impact (EIP reservation + transfer)

alex.sr: Customer also asked about SNI/TLS-inspect appliances on their egress. If they inspect TLS, will PrivateLink break anything?

marvin.net: PrivateLink preserves TLS to our endpoint; if they terminate TLS for inspection, they'll see client certs only if we allow. We recommend mTLS between customer and our endpoint if they TLS-inspect. For SNI preservation: ensure proxy forwards SNI or use IP-based allowlist instead of FQDN.

jorge.ae: Action items for us: 1) provide a short pricing note for EIP reservation and monthly bandwidth impact; 2) return a firewall snippet + clarifying options; 3) schedule quick call between their netops and our netops.

priya.se: I'll draft the pricing note. For a Dedicated Private deployment with 2 reserved EIPs + 10TB/month transfer, rough estimate: EIP reservation $500/month, bandwidth per TB at our standard private rate — I'll confirm exact numbers with billing.

dana.sec: I'll attach our security questionnaire answers about network isolation, KMS for keys, and logging retention after the thread. For now note: we support customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs to S3 (can be forwarded to their SIEM).

marvin.net: For the firewall snippet that preserves client IP via on-host proxy (option C), here's a quick example for the customer's infra team to run as a sidecar:

```
# nginx reverse proxy config (example to forward client IP)
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  proxy_pass https://redwood-internal:443;
}
```

alex.sr: Perfect. Can we get firm pricing + EIP contract language by EOD tomorrow? Customer is trying to finalize their procurement window.

priya.se: I'll get numbers from billing now. @marvin.net can you confirm EIP pool availability and any quota ops tickets needed?

marvin.net: Confirmed — we have capacity for small Dedicated pools. If they want global redundant EIPs across regions, that needs legal canary and longer lead time. For a single-region POC it's fine. I'll open quota ticket after we get customer account ID.

jorge.ae: I'll book the call with their netops for tomorrow 11am PT and invite everyone.

infra-bot: Reminder: please attach the standard Private deployment network runbook to the calendar invite — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privatedeploy-network

alex.sr: Thanks team. I'll send the customer a concise options email (PrivateLink+EIPs vs VPN/TGW). Will loop back when billing numbers are in. :thumbsup:
